question: How Does a Diode Rectifier Circuit Work?
body_html:
A diode rectifier circuit converts AC to pulsating DC because a diode conducts in only one direction. A half wave rectifier uses one diode, while centre tap and bridge full wave types use two or four diodes.

Half wave gives Vdc = 0.318 × Vpeak and full wave gives Vdc = 0.636 × Vpeak. Example: for Vpeak = 100 V, half wave averages 31.8 V and full wave 63.6 V. A filter capacitor smooths the ripple.
